observations.note: 'Delist' → 'Retirar' is the right per-locale call. Shipped es already uses retirar for withdrawing public content ('...pero no retira nada que ya sea público', ui.hub.subscriptions.enable_public) and reserves eliminar for real deletion (ui.agents.dialogs.delete.question); the three delist control strings share the verb root, so speech control finds the confirm from the aria name. The reversible action is described honestly in the body.

'Get' → 'Descargar' is not drift: shipped es names the hub download action descargar (ui.hub.skills.download 'Descargar', ui.hub.skills.pull_title 'Descargar {item} desde {source}'), the detail page's counterpart in this same namespace is 'Descargar el agente', and the aria 'Descargar {name}' must contain the visible label. 'Obtener' exists in shipped es for non-download senses (ui.onboarding.search.row.get_your 'Obtener {name}'), so using it here would split one action across two verbs.

Age joins checked against the emitting code, not guessed. card.updated and both detail metadata lines pass {age} from hubAge → commentAge (comment-age.ts), whose es values in ui.hub.comments.age.* already contain 'hace' ('hace {count} días'). So they render 'actualizado hace 3 días', 'Creado: hace 3 días (10 oct 2026)' and 'Última modificación: hace 3 días (10 oct 2026)': no doubled preposition, no missing one, and the leading lowercase 'actualizado' follows the sidecar's instruction. {date} is preformatted by formatCalendarDate and is never hand-patterned here.

The three unknown-state sentences preserve the sidecar's core requirement — a failed read is never asserted as 'not favourited' or 'not liked'. The wording spells out the absence in plain Spanish ('esto no significa que no esté en favoritos', 'no se muestra si te gusta este agente o lo tienes en favoritos') rather than calquing a 'viewer state' noun, which has no natural es equivalent. Reads as native product explanation, and the two card mirrors stay parallel.

Register and typography are consistent across all 41 values: tú throughout ('Inicia sesión', 'Puedes volver a subirlo', 'tus favoritos', 'no te guste'); infinitive action labels ('Descargar', 'Retirar', 'Añadir', 'Quitar', 'Dar', 'Volver'); sentence case; no exclamation; curly “ ” quotes; the one whole question carries '¿…?'; no space before colons; no NBSP/NNBSP. Lowercase 'del hub' in delist_body mirrors English's generic 'the hub' and shipped 'Subir al hub' (ui.agents.dialogs.menu.upload); capitalised 'Hub de agentes' in back_aria/delist_tooltip mirrors the shipped es navigation label (ui.shell.sidebar_navigation.agent_hub, ui.command_palette.use_palette_sources.agent_hub), so the two forms are the source's own named/generic distinction, not drift.

Terminology against the glossary and shipped es: 'agente' for agent; 'Radient' kept as the product name in the four strings that name it; no tool names, flags, paths, commands or machine tokens occur in this namespace, so nothing needed keeping byte-identical beyond 'Radient' and the {placeholders}. 'equipo' in download_tooltip means this machine, matching the shipped es installation vocabulary (51 occurrences of 'tu equipo' or 'este equipo' across shipped es, e.g. ui.common.updates), and the team sense of equipo does not occur in this namespace.

The source's own tension between 'Permanently delist' (delist_tooltip) and 'You can upload it again later' (delist_body) is rendered faithfully, not amplified: 'de forma permanente' describes removal from the public listing, and the body states the re-upload route. catalogue_no_answer is a lead sentence joined by a single space to the shared backendLoadErrorMessage diagnosis/remedy, so its final period produces correct punctuation, not a double stop.
